instructions.content: Inspect the diff or description to identify whether it adds new behaviour, fixes existing behaviour, or neither.
instructions.original_snippets: Inspect the change — read the diff or the user's description. Identify whether it adds new behaviour, fixes existing behaviour, or neither.

instructions.content: Use the type decision rules to disambiguate refactor vs feat, fix vs refactor, perf vs refactor, and treat chore as the last resort.
instructions.original_snippets: refactor vs feat: does the user gain new capability? If yes -> feat ... chore vs anything else: if another type fits, use it -- chore is the last resort

instructions.content: Split a change spanning multiple types into multiple atomic commits instead of picking one type for all of it.
instructions.original_snippets: Multiple types needed? Split into multiple commits (see Atomic Commits)

instructions.content: Pick the scope from the module, package, or layer name; omit scope when the change is cross-cutting; use the project's fixed scope vocabulary when one exists.
instructions.original_snippets: Pick the scope - use the module, package, or layer name (e.g. auth, checkout, api). Omit scope when the change is truly cross-cutting.

instructions.content: Draft the header in imperative mood, lowercase, at or under 72 characters, and verify it completes 'If applied, this commit will <header>.'
instructions.original_snippets: Draft the header - imperative mood, lowercase, <= 72 characters. Verify with: "If applied, this commit will <header>."

instructions.content: Add a commit body only when the why is not obvious from the diff, and wrap body lines at 72 characters.
instructions.original_snippets: Add a body if needed - only when the why is not obvious. Explain the reasoning, not the implementation. Wrap at 72 characters.

instructions.content: Add a Closes footer for issue references and a BREAKING CHANGE footer whenever the public API surface changes; always pair '!' with a BREAKING CHANGE footer.
instructions.original_snippets: Add footers - Closes: #N for issue references; BREAKING CHANGE: <description> whenever the public API surface changes. Always pair ! with a BREAKING CHANGE: footer.

instructions.content: Verify the message before committing with git commit --dry-run or the project's commitlint hook.
instructions.original_snippets: Verify before committing - run git commit --dry-run or your local commitlint hook to catch formatting violations before they enter history.

instructions.content: Present the finished commit message in a fenced code block with no extra commentary, ready to paste.
instructions.original_snippets: Agent output format: Present the commit message in a fenced code block with no extra commentary, ready to paste

instructions.content: NEVER write the header in past tense; it completes the sentence 'If applied, this commit will...' and past tense breaks that contract.
instructions.original_snippets: NEVER use past tense in the description - WHY: The header completes the sentence "If applied, this commit will..." - past tense breaks that contract

instructions.content: NEVER use chore as a catch-all type for features, refactors, or docs, since it hides semantic meaning from changelog generators.
instructions.original_snippets: NEVER use chore as a catch-all - WHY: chore is for maintenance tasks not covered by other types ... Using it for features, refactors, or docs hides semantic meaning from changelog generators.

instructions.content: NEVER exceed 72 characters in the header, because git log, GitHub PR titles, and CI tools truncate longer headers.
instructions.original_snippets: NEVER exceed 72 characters in the header - WHY: Git log, GitHub PR titles, and most CI tools truncate at 72 characters.

instructions.content: NEVER omit the BREAKING CHANGE footer when the API surface changes; the '!' suffix alone is not sufficient for all tooling.
instructions.original_snippets: NEVER omit BREAKING CHANGE: footer when the API surface changes - WHY: The ! suffix alone is not sufficient for all tooling.

instructions.content: NEVER put implementation details in the header; the header is the summary visible in git log --oneline, details belong in the body.
instructions.original_snippets: NEVER put implementation details in the header - WHY: The header is the commit summary visible in git log --oneline. Implementation details belong in the body.

instructions.content: NEVER bundle unrelated changes in one commit; a commit spanning multiple concerns cannot be cherry-picked or reverted cleanly.
instructions.original_snippets: NEVER bundle unrelated changes in one commit - WHY: A commit that spans multiple concerns can't be cherry-picked or reverted cleanly.

instructions.content: The description portion of the header must be imperative mood, lowercase, with no trailing period.
instructions.original_snippets: Description: imperative mood (add not added), lowercase, no trailing period, <= 72 characters

instructions.content: Separate the body from the header by exactly one blank line, wrap body lines at 72 characters, and explain why not what.
instructions.original_snippets: Body: separated by one blank line, lines wrapped at 72 characters, explains why not what

instructions.content: Write footers in 'Token: value' format, e.g. Closes: #123 or BREAKING CHANGE: description.
instructions.original_snippets: Footers: Token: value format (e.g. Closes: #123, BREAKING CHANGE: description)

instructions.content: Signal breaking changes by appending '!' after type/scope and/or adding a BREAKING CHANGE footer, which triggers a MAJOR version bump.
instructions.original_snippets: Breaking changes: append ! after type/scope (feat!:) and/or add a BREAKING CHANGE: footer - triggers a MAJOR version bump.

instructions.content: Skip this skill when the project explicitly avoids Conventional Commits or enforces a custom pattern via a project-specific hook; do not override confirmed project conventions.
instructions.original_snippets: When not to use: skip this skill if the project explicitly avoids Conventional Commits ... Do not override confirmed project conventions.
